newsitem.title: USA: Texas Panhandle cattle trade at $62, off $1 -USDA.
newsitem.headline: Texas Panhandle cattle trade at $62, off $1 -USDA.

text.p: U.S. Texas Panhandle feedlot cattle sold at $62.00 per cwt in light trading on Monday, down $1.00 from last week, USDA reported.
About 3,700 steers and heifers likely to grade select and choice sold from two feedlots, a USDA source said.

However, private sources at Plains-area feedyards said some bids at $62.00 were passed by owners who were pricing cattle at $63.00 to mostly $64.00, with a few at $65.00. No sales were reported in Kansas or Nebraska near midday, they said.

Weakness in Texas Panhandle prices was linked to a large supply of market-ready cattle, with this week's showlists inflated by some unsold cattle carried from last week's holiday-shortened sales, feedlot sources said.

The showlist for the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area this week was estimated near 104,000 head, up 17,000 from last week, sources said. The Kansas showlist was estimated near 91,000 head, down 3,500 from last week.
Some cattle feeders said despite the early $62 sales, they expected cattle would sell this week about steady at $63 amid retail fill-in demand following the long holiday weekend.
